_comment: One full POST /allocate response per profile in user_profiles.json. Each entry pairs an AllocationExplanation with the InstrumentWeight[] for the stocks bucket and the MF bucket, exactly as CLAUDE.md §4.2 says /allocate should return. These are hand-set to be *directionally* consistent with each profile's risk thermometer (via the FD floor/ceiling formula in CLAUDE.md §5.3) -- not run through a real optimizer, just plausible enough to build and demo a UI against.

key_drivers: Risk thermometer of 12/100 pushes the FD floor/ceiling toward the top of its band (~70-80%).
3-year horizon favors capital preservation over equity's longer-run edge.
Debt mutual fund allocation adds a small real-return cushion beyond a pure FD position.
20% tax slab reduces FD net yield -- part of why post-tax return sits below the nominal FD rate.

mf_weights.display_name: ICICI Prudential Short Term Debt Fund

key_drivers: Risk thermometer of 52/100 lands FD allocation near the middle of its floor/ceiling band.
Banking sector preference concentrated the stock pie chart in HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank, with one IT holding kept in after correlation-based dedup for diversification.
7-year horizon supports a meaningful but not maximal equity tilt.
30% tax slab makes the LTCG-taxed equity sleeve relatively more attractive post-tax than the FD sleeve.
Risk thermometer of 88/100 pushes the FD floor to ~0%, so no FD instruments were selected (user also excluded FD from instruments).
IT sector preference concentrated the stock pie chart in TCS and Infosys, with one banking holding kept in after correlation-based dedup.
15-year horizon comfortably absorbs equity volatility for a higher expected post-tax real return.
30% tax slab plus a >12-month LTCG assumption keeps the effective equity tax drag low relative to FD/debt-MF interest taxed at slab rate.
